_comment: Task descriptor list. Each task = one minimal action compared clone-vs-real-Word. The runner derives file paths by convention: probe=parity/probes/<id>-pilot-probe.js, com=parity/ground-truth/realword_<id>.ps1, fixtures=parity/fixtures/{wc,rw}-<id>.docx. realword_method: 'com' (scriptable, COM==ribbon) or 'vsto' (gallery/style action where COM != ribbon -> needs real UI capture). Run a tier batch with: python parity/engines/run.py --tier T0 --capture (Word closed).

_flow_verifier_candidates._note: T0 clipboard/flow controls with NO clean single-action OOXML delta — DEFERRED to the UI-flow verifier, NOT the OOXML diff (would block/pollute the batch).

items.why: Copy produces NO document delta (clipboard only).
Needs a selection precondition; the delta is a deletion, not an additive feature.
Needs a clipboard precondition; output depends on clipboard contents/paste-mode.

tasks.note: Bold mark on a run. COM == ribbon.
Italic mark on a run. COM == ribbon.

tasks.action: select a word, apply single underline
tasks.note: Single underline (w:u w:val=single). COM Font.Underline=1 == ribbon.

tasks.action: select a word, set font family to Arial
tasks.note: Font family (w:rFonts ascii/hAnsi=Arial). COM Font.Name == ribbon font picker.

tasks.action: select a word, set font size to 14pt
tasks.note: Font size (w:sz w:val=28 half-points). COM Font.Size == ribbon size box.

tasks.action: apply a default bullet list to the paragraph
tasks.note: WARNING (COM != ribbon): numbering.xml IS now diffed, and the large numbering.xml delta is a COM-method ARTIFACT — COM ListFormat.ApplyBulletDefault() writes a singleLevel abstractNum while the ribbon Bullets button (and the clone) write a multilevel one, so the clone's extra levels read as 'extra' even though the clone is MORE ribbon-faithful than this COM ground truth. A TRUE numbering.xml comparison needs a vsto/UIA ribbon capture. The document.xml ground truth (numPr + pStyle ListParagraph) IS faithful — and the document.xml gap (missing pStyle ListParagraph + numPr child order) is now FIXED by feature 023, so the BODY is at parity; the remaining diff is PURELY the numbering.xml COM-artifact.
Left is Word's DEFAULT alignment, so Word may emit NO explicit w:jc — a clone that emits jc=left over-emits (real signal).
Center alignment (w:jc w:val=center). COM ParagraphFormat.Alignment=1 == ribbon.

tasks.action: select a word, set font color to red
tasks.note: Font color (w:color w:val=FF0000). COM Font.Color=255 == ribbon Font Color.

tasks.action: select a word, apply yellow highlight
tasks.note: WARNING (COM != ribbon, adversarial-review-confirmed): COM HighlightColorIndex stamps the highlight on the PARAGRAPH-MARK rPr too; the ribbon Highlighter on a word selection does NOT (proven: bold via the same Range(0,7) emits no para-mark rPr and is 0/0). So the 3 'missing' (pPr/rPr/highlight) are a COM-method ground-truth artifact — the clone's run-level w:highlight is FAITHFUL; REAL ribbon parity = 0/0. Recapture via vsto/UIA to confirm.

tasks.action: apply a default numbered list to the paragraph
tasks.note: WARNING (COM != ribbon): numbering.xml IS now diffed, and the large numbering.xml delta is a COM-method ARTIFACT — COM ListFormat.ApplyNumberDefault() writes a singleLevel (1-level) abstractNum, but the ribbon Numbering button (and the clone) write a multilevel definition, so the clone's extra levels read as 'extra' even though the clone is MORE ribbon-faithful than this COM ground truth. A TRUE numbering.xml comparison needs a vsto/UIA ribbon capture. The document.xml ground truth (numPr + pStyle ListParagraph) IS faithful — and the document.xml gap (missing pStyle ListParagraph + numPr child order) is now FIXED by feature 023, so the BODY is at parity; the remaining diff is PURELY the numbering.xml COM-artifact.
Justify (w:jc w:val=both). COM ParagraphFormat.Alignment=3 (wdAlignParagraphJustify) == ribbon.

tasks.note: Line spacing 2.0 (w:spacing w:line=480 w:lineRule=auto). COM ParagraphFormat.LineSpacingRule=2 (wdLineSpaceDouble) == ribbon.
